topics.title: Restricting domains: principal branches of sin⁻¹ and cos⁻¹

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a trigonometric function must be restricted to an interval on which it is one-one and onto before it can be inverted.
State the domain and principal value range of sin⁻¹.
State the domain and principal value range of cos⁻¹ and identify valid branches.

topics.title: Principal branches of cosec⁻¹, sec⁻¹, tan⁻¹ and cot⁻¹

concepts.learning_objective: State the domains and principal value ranges of cosec⁻¹ and sec⁻¹ and explain the excluded values.
State the domains and principal value ranges of tan⁻¹ and cot⁻¹.
Find principal values of inverse trigonometric functions and evaluate expressions built from them.
Distinguish sin⁻¹ x from (sin x)⁻¹ and obtain the graph of an inverse function by reflection in the line y = x.

topics.title: Composition properties of inverse trigonometric functions

concepts.learning_objective: Use sin(sin⁻¹ x) = x and sin⁻¹(sin x) = x with their conditions on x.
Evaluate expressions such as sin⁻¹(sin θ) when θ lies outside the principal branch.

topics.title: Writing inverse trigonometric expressions in the simplest form

concepts.learning_objective: Choose a suitable substitution such as x = sin θ, x = a sin θ or x = sec θ to simplify an inverse trigonometric expression.
Simplify expressions in cos x and sin x using half-angle identities to reach tan⁻¹(tan θ).
